content.text:
Yes—the fix resolves the accepted timing-evidence defect. I found no concrete remaining issue in the timestamp change; logical-clock semantics, delivery/drop ordering, and existing deadlines remain unchanged.

- Patch 0013 now locks before sampling `actual`, then determines connection state, delivers or drops, emits the report, and unlocks (`patches/norns/0013-midi-connection-lifecycle.patch:114–123`). The generator matches (`scripts/prepare_midi_hotplug.py:37–42`). The reconstructed baseline/candidate sources differ only by this movement; both source/function hashes match the retained report, and the patch hash matches the dependency lock.
- The test extracts and compiles the actual function (`tests/midi_arrival_contention.py:17–24`). Its semaphore and real mutex establish contention; both branches check timestamp placement and delivery/report behavior (`tests/midi_arrival_contention.c:29–50`). Retained results show baseline timestamps approximately **250 ms early**, versus candidate timestamps **46,320 ns and 28,460 ns after the release marker** (`artifacts/hotplug/arrival-contention-20260909-162712/report.json:9–18`).
- Logical time still reads `emu_clock_now()`, an atomic logical counter; the clock advances after synchronous scheduled delivery returns (`src/runtime/native_clock/emu_clock.c:24,54,85`). No deadline or admission tolerance changed.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** I verified source and retained evidence without rerunning tests; corrected whole-runtime checks were not yet recorded in H06’s completion file, so this closes the focused native-boundary finding only.
